key_insight: RoSHI combines low-cost sparse IMUs with Project Aria egocentric glasses to produce full 3D human pose and body-shape estimates in a metric global frame, enabling robust, portable capture of long-horizon interactions in the wild.
problem_solved: Existing human-data collection approaches for robot learning force trade-offs between portability, occlusion robustness, and global consistency; RoSHI resolves this by fusing complementary wearable sensors to deliver accurate, globally-referenced body reconstructions from an egocentric setup.
method: Hybrid wearable hardware: integrate sparse, low-cost inertial measurement units (IMUs) with Project Aria egocentric cameras/glasses to capture complementary signals.
Sensor fusion pipeline: align and fuse visual egocentric cues with IMU motion data to estimate full 3D pose and body shape in a metric global coordinate frame.
Design-for-in-the-wild: optimize for portability and occlusion robustness to support long-horizon, real-world human interaction data collection for robot learning.
impact: Enables scalable collection of rich, globally-consistent human behavior datasets needed for robot learning and embodied AI, while reducing sensitivity to occlusion and improving portability of capture rigs.
visual_elements: Illustration of the RoSHI wearable: Project Aria glasses + sparse IMU modules on a person (annotated sensor types).
Pipeline flowchart: egocentric video + IMU data → sensor fusion → global 3D pose & body-shape output.
Before/after comparison: occluded scenes where vision-only fails vs successful RoSHI reconstruction.
Example overlays: reconstructed full-body mesh in a global coordinate frame placed within a real scene map.
paper_title: RoSHI: A Versatile Robot-oriented Suit for Human Data In-the-Wild
paper_authors: Wenjing Margaret Mao, Jefferson Ng, Luyang Hu, Daniel Gehrig, Antonio Loquercio
